claims.text: A 10 μm Al2O3 coating can be deposited by plasma spraying onto cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 coating will improve the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
The oxygen-resistance improvement will occur at 1000 °C in air over a 100-hour exposure.
The coated alloy will retain useful mechanical performance at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Al2O3 acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the coating reduces oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The coating will reduce the oxidation rate by 30% relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will increase yield strength at 1000 °C by 10% relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Coating performance may depend on deposition method, coating thickness, and substrate surface roughness.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis promises no sacrifice in mechanical performance, but the falsification rule permits a yield-strength decrease of up to 5% without falsifying it.
